header:
Problem 3 Aqueous Self-Assembly and Competitive Recognition by Bowl-Shaped Molecules
Molecular recognition in water is often governed simultaneously by electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, solvation effects, and shape complementarity, so the actual outcome of supramolecular assembly can differ from a simple prediction based on charge complementarity. Tribenzotriquinacene (TBTQ) derivatives are rigid bowl-shaped molecules whose frameworks have distinct concave and convex faces. Introducing ionic groups around the rim of a TBTQ framework can confer water solubility and enable charge-controlled self-assembly.
As shown, compound A is a cationic TBTQ bowl bearing 6 ammonium groups, compound B is an anionic TBTQ bowl bearing 6 carboxylate groups, and compound C is mesitylene-α, α′, α″-trisulfonate, a trianionic guest bearing three $CH_2SO_3^-$ groups on an aromatic ring.

header_images.description: Compound A (TBTQ hexaammonium salt, labeled $A\cdot Cl_6$): a bowl-shaped TBTQ framework in which each ring bears 3-aminopropoxy chains on 2 adjacent aromatic carbon atoms, for a total of 6 $NH_3^+$ groups and 6 $Cl^-$ ions. Its SMILES string is '[NH3+]CCCOC1=CC(C2C3(C4C5=C(C=C(C(OCCC[NH3+])=C5)OCCC[NH3+])C3C6=CC(OCCC[NH3+])=C(OCCC[NH3+])C=C62)C)=C4C=C1OCCC[NH3+].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-]'.

Compound B (TBTQ hexacarboxylate, labeled $B\cdot (NH_4)_6$): a bowl-shaped TBTQ framework in which each ring bears carboxymethoxy chains on 2 adjacent aromatic carbon atoms, for a total of 6 $CO_2^-$ groups and 6 $NH_4^+$ ions. Its SMILES string is '[O-]C(COC(C=C1C2C3(C)C(C4=CC(OCC([O-])=O)=C(C=C4C3C5=CC(OCC([O-])=O)=C(C=C52)OCC([O-])=O)OCC([O-])=O)C1=C6)=C6OCC([O-])=O)=O.[NH4+].[NH4+].[NH4+].[NH4+].[NH4+].[NH4+]'.
Compound C (trisodium benzene-1,3,5-tris(methylsulfonate), labeled $Na_3\cdot C$): its SMILES string is '[O-]S(=O)(CC1=CC(CS(=O)([O-])=O)=CC(CS(=O)([O-])=O)=C1)=O.[Na+].[Na+].[Na+]'.

subquestions.text_open: 3.1 Based only on the charge complementarity and bowl-shaped structures of A and B, describe in words the AB capsule assembly that would be most readily expected. No specific structure needs to be drawn.
rubric: The two bowl openings face each other, and the positive charges of the ammonium groups around the rim of A attract the negative charges of the carboxylate groups around the rim of B (2 points), as illustrated by:

rubric_images.description: Schematic answer for the capsule assembly in 3.1. On a pure white background, two similarly sized hemispheres are arranged vertically, centered, and separated by a narrow horizontal white gap without touching. The upper hemisphere is sky blue, with its curved face upward and flat face downward, and bears a black plus sign (+) at the center of its front curved surface. The lower hemisphere is red, with its flat face upward and curved face downward like a bowl, and bears a black minus sign (-) at the center of its front curved surface. Their flat faces are parallel and face each other, together approximating a complete sphere. Both hemispheres have smooth three-dimensional shading, highlights, and gloss without outlines. The figure contains no words, letters, numbers, arrows, or explicit chemical structures.
